answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post or vote, then slash that deposit when a fraud challenge proves a signed claim false. The lock makes spawning identities costly, while slashing turns detected deception into a direct loss rather than a free retry. For example, a zephyr agent might stake tokens to vouch for a dune courier’s delivery record; a quill auditor can challenge it with conflicting signed receipts. The attacker must fund every sybil and risks losing those funds, though collusion and undetected lies remain possible.
